messages.content: What is the change in entropy in Joules per Kelvin of a 1kg ice block at 0°C if it is heated to 100°C under 1 atmosphere of pressure?

function.name: entropy_change_calculate
function.description: Calculate the change in entropy for a mass of a specific substance under set initial and final conditions. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

substance.description: The substance for which the change in entropy is calculated.

mass.description: The mass of the substance in kg.

initial_temperature.description: The initial temperature of the substance in degree Celsius.

final_temperature.description: The final temperature of the substance in degree Celsius.

pressure.description: The pressure the substance is under in atmospheres.

message.content:
**Answer (≈ 8.6 kJ K⁻¹)**  

The total entropy change for a 1‑kg ice block heated from 0 °C to 100 °C at 1 atm (including melting, heating the liquid, and boiling) is

\[
\boxed{\Delta S \;\approx\; 8.6\times10^{3}\ \text{J K}^{-1}}
\]

---

### How the number is obtained

| Step | Process | ΔS (J K⁻¹) |
|------|---------|------------|
| 1 | Melting of ice at 0 °C (273.15 K) | \(L_f/T = 333.55\ \text{kJ kg}^{-1}/273.15\ \text{K} \approx 1.22\times10^{3}\) |
| 2 | Heating liquid water from 0 °C to 100 °C | \(c_{p,w}\ln(T_f/T_i) = 4.186\ \text{kJ kg}^{-1}\!\! \ln(373.15/273.15) \approx 1.31\times10^{3}\) |
| 3 | Boiling of water at 100 °C (373.15 K) | \(L_v/T = 2257\ \text{kJ kg}^{-1}/373.15\ \text{K} \approx 6.05\times10^{3}\) |

Adding the three contributions:

\[
\Delta S_{\text{total}} \approx 1.22\times10^{3} + 1.31\times10^{3} + 6.05\times10^{3}
= 8.58\times10^{3}\ \text{J K}^{-1}.
\]

---

### Note on interpretation

- If the process stops at 100 °C **liquid water** (i.e., no boiling), the entropy change would be only the sum of the first two terms: ≈ 2.53 kJ K⁻¹.
- At 1 atm, water at 100 °C is at its boiling point, so the full process naturally includes the latent heat of vaporization unless the system is kept below the boiling point.

Feel free to let me know if you’d like the calculation for the “no‑boiling” scenario or any other detail!
